(Characters nearby (from nearest to furthest): Brynjolf, Daegon, Lydia, Serana, Maramal) (MJR: Actually, I'm looking for this old guy hiding out in Riften.; Brynjolf: Ah. Expecting free information, eh? Help me deal with business first, then we'll see how I can help you. Besides, you look like your pockets are a little light on coin, am I right?)
Vulwulf Snow-Shod: Late hour for a fisherman to be in the tavern, Bolli. Trouble at home keeping you from your bed?

Bolli: Trouble at home? Nivenor's been spending more time at the market than in our bed. A man starts to wonder if his own hearth is worth returning to. Vulwulf Snow-Shod: A familiar tale, Bolli. My own wife has taken to visiting the Temple of Dibella more often than she visits my chambers. These Riften women have strange ideas about devotion.

Vulwulf Snow-Shod: I see my son Asgeir has wandered in. Probably looking for coin to throw away on drink and whores. Bolli: At least he's spending his own coin. My wife spends mine well enough for the both of us. You'd think Maramal would have a word with her about wasting good septims on perfumes that smell like a marsh flower's backside.

Bolli: Sapphire's giving that mercenary Marcurio an earful again. That girl's got a tongue sharper than a filleting knife. Vulwulf Snow-Shod: She's got good reason for it. Half the men in Riften treat her like she's part of the trade down at the Bunkhouse rather than a proper businesswoman.

Bolli: Aye, but there's truth in what she says. Haelga's Bunkhouse draws a certain crowd, and folks paint everyone with the same brush. I ought to know. Vulwulf Snow-Shod: You'd think a man of the cloth like Maramal would have more influence on the city's morals. Instead he just sits in his temple counting donations while the whole of Riften sinks into Dibella's embrace.

Vulwulf Snow-Shod: Is that a septim on the floor by the stairs? At this hour, most honest folk are abed. Could be someone's been gambling in the back room. Bolli: Or dropping coin during other activities.

Bolli: Well, this tavern floor's seen more action tonight than my marriage bed in a month. I think I'll take my leave of this conversation before my tongue gets me into more trouble than my coin purse can handle. Vulwulf Snow-Shod: Wise man. I'll watch the door a while longer. If Brynjolf's game is what I think it is, morning's going to bring quite a stir to the marketplace.
(The location is now Bee and Barb.) (Characters nearby (from nearest to furthest): Keerava, Serana, Daegon, Asgeir Snow-Shod, Lydia)
Vulwulf Snow-Shod: The fire's dying down and the hour's late. Not many left but the usual hangers-on. Bolli: Aye, Asgeir's still nursing a tankard over there.

Serana: What a charming morning in Riften - the scent of fish, corruption, and regret all mingling together like a fine mead. Makes me almost miss Hamelyn's love potion.

Serana: Maven Black-Briar looks like she swallowed a bee and found it too spicy. That symbol must be quite the party favor to get her knickers in a twist. Bolli: Aye, when Maven gets that look in her eye, someone's about to lose more than just their business.

Shadr: I heard Sabjorn's mead was going sour months ago. Surprised it took this long for someone to call in the debts. Bolli: Sour mead and sour deals go hand in hand in Riften. That's why I stick to fish - they only smell bad when they're fresh out the water. Serana: Speaking from experience with bad deals, I'd say that symbol looks like it was drawn by someone with trembling hands and a guilty conscience. Or maybe that's just the standard handwriting of people who owe Maven money.
